A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-Critic, with matching core sections and appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and qualitative examples support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of trained LLaVA-Critic models, including pointwise and pairwise judgments, preference-learning experiments, and iterative DPO results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds inference-time selection results, training-data ablations, visual-capability evaluations, and additional baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 adds critic-guided best-of-five inference: generate five responses from the DPO-trained LLaVA-OV-7B model and use LLaVA-Critic-7B to select one (Section 5.2). The critic architecture, cross-entropy training, pairwise reward aggregation, and iterative DPO procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training sources and evaluation datasets remain the same. The new ablations, direct critic evaluations, and best-of-five experiment reuse existing task coverage. The comprehensive-benchmark caption changes from five to four, but retains the same MME perception/cognition, MMB-en, MM-Vet, and MMStar columns.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaMA3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct to the judge comparisons, and GPT-4o as a DPO reward provider in Table 13. Table 7 also compares best-of-five selection with random sampling. These are targeted extensions of the retained comparison methods.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include best-of-five inference with temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.9, critic training on selected data components, and direct visual-task evaluation of critic checkpoints. The existing judge sample counts, metrics, critic-training settings, and three-round DPO protocol are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-data ablations separating pointwise, pairwise, and tie supervision (Appendix C.1, Table 8), plus checks of visual-capability retention after critic tuning (Appendix C.4, Table 12). These substantially extend the analysis of data design and tuning side effects beyond v1's model/data scaling and DPO-round comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Multiple candidate responses and successive DPO training rounds do not constitute reported repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for new comparators, data ablations, capability retention, and inference selection. Table 7 reports best-of-five scores of 102.0 and 74.8, versus random-sampling scores of 100.3 and 71.6. It also revises the LLaVA-v1.5-7B MM-Vet value from 30.5 to 31.1 (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 5). Most matched earlier results are retained.

T1.justification: The training-example definitions and Section 4.3 reward-aggregation mathematics are substantively unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs; the added ablation explanations are conceptual interpretations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the 113k critic dataset, an open generalist multimodal evaluator, and useful reward signals for preference learning. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline claims or their novelty scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that relative-ranking supervision lacks absolute-judgment information and that tie examples discourage fixation on small quality differences (Appendix C.1). It also narrows the MLLM-as-a-Judge superiority statement from all baselines except GPT models to baselines of comparable model size.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new inference-search sampling settings and reports an approximate $690 GPT-4o cost for three DPO rounds. It also omits v1's Section 3.1 footnote specifying that VLFeedback GPT-4V responses supply reference answers for both RefoMB and WildVision prompts. That omission establishes a documentation change, not a changed data-curation procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Stiennon et al., Learning to Summarize with Human Feedback, to support best-of-n sampling. The related-work discussion and positioning against Prometheus-Vision and prior preference-learning methods remain substantively stable; Qwen2-VL was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections and shortens several passages while retaining the main section sequence and most prose. Appendix C gains subsections for the added analyses, and the existing Kendall's Tau discussion moves there. This is a limited narrative revision.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the paper into two columns, resizes figures, and rearranges tables. The Kendall's Tau block of v1 Table 2 becomes appendix Table 10, preference-learning Tables 5 and 6 exchange order, and new Tables 7, 8, and 12 display added experiments. Figure 2 is compressed vertically with adjusted tick spacing.

improvement.justification: v2 fills focused validation gaps through data-component ablations, checks of retained visual abilities, and a direct GPT-4o reward comparison (Tables 8, 12, and 13). It also qualifies an overly broad baseline-comparison statement. These additions strengthen an already extensively evaluated approach and provide a limited overall quality improvement.
